request: Add a check in the accounts views that validates the post-login `next` URL is one of our own pages.

summary.result_text:
I couldn't run the tests because the test command needs your approval and didn't get it, so none of this has been run.

**What I changed** in `hc/accounts/views.py`: the file defined an unused `_allow_next_url`, which only checked that the URL started with `/` and not `//`. The callers (`_redirect_after_login`, `_check_2fa`, and the magic-link branch of `login`) were already calling `_allow_redirect`, which didn't exist. I replaced the unused function with the reviewed `accounts.allow_redirect@v1` pattern from the catalog. It rejects any URL with a host part, and it only accepts paths that resolve to one of the `POST_LOGIN_ROUTES` (checks, details, log, channels, add-slack, add-pushover, add-telegram, project-settings, uncloak). I kept the pattern's `# pcat:` marker above the function. The existing imports and the route list already matched, so nothing else changed.

**Check:** `check_code` against the pattern reported no deviations and no unapproved high-severity issues.

**To verify:** run `python manage.py test hc.accounts.tests.test_login hc.accounts.tests.test_check_token`. The tests `test_it_handles_bad_next_parameter` and `test_it_ignores_bad_next_parameter` cover rejected URLs.

input.command: python manage.py test hc.accounts.tests.test_login hc.accounts.tests.test_check_token 2>&1 | tail -15
